title: Battery management and DC protection for a storage plant
description:
Work package: battery management system (BMS) and DC string protection for a grid-connected lithium iron phosphate storage plant in Germany. The system team has closed the plant design and hands it over; the plant itself cannot change. Your team designs the rack BMS (one per string, identical for every rack) and writes down the requirements it derives.

Stakeholder needs:
  SN-1: usable energy 2.300 MWh at the connection point (requirement including the project margin) at end of service life, 1 h duration, within the cell manufacturer's recommended SOC window.
  SN-2: prequalification for frequency containment reserve (FCR) in Germany with 1.8 MW, symmetric.
  SN-3: DC bus of a PCS ready within 5 s of a start command.
  SN-4: cells operated within the cell manufacturer's safety limits at all times, including faults.
  SN-5: lowest BMS and protection cost for the plant.

Handover from the system team (end of life where it matters):
  19 strings (one per rack) of 368 cells in series: 23 modules of 16 cells, 6 temperature sensors per module.
  String current at rated power 130.8 A; string voltage at full charge 1343.2 V.
  Cell capacity at end of life 220.9 Ah. SOC window 10-90%.
  Usable energy at the connection point at end of life over the full window, net of auxiliaries: 3.6213 MWh; auxiliary energy during a full 1 h discharge: 0.0724 MWh.
  PCS: 4 x PCS-1 (1100 kVA), strings on one PCS share its DC bus; DC-link capacitance 4.8 mF per PCS.
  String fuse FU-10: gBat, 400 A. Pre-arcing time by multiple of rated current: 1.6 x: 4210.0, 2 x: 314.0, 3 x: 35.2, 4 x: 5.31, 5 x: 1.68, 7 x: 0.219, 10 x: 0.0339, 15 x: 0.00883, 20 x: 0.00339 s.
  Rack controller interfaces: 2 CAN buses (PCS, energy management), 6 analogue channels (current, voltages on both sides of the contactor, insulation monitoring, spares).

Cell datasheet (LFP prismatic, 280 Ah, 3.2 V nominal, charge to 3.65 V, continuous 0.5 C):
  Open-circuit voltage by SOC %: 0: 2.951, 5: 3.172, 10: 3.21, 20: 3.249, 30: 3.273, 40: 3.286, 50: 3.289, 60: 3.295, 70: 3.314, 80: 3.329, 85: 3.335, 90: 3.334, 95: 3.343, 100: 3.401 V.
  Safety limit: above 3.75 V the cell must be disconnected within 150 ms.
  Short-time current limit by multiple of 1 C: 2 C: 70.4, 3 C: 12.4, 5 C: 1.66, 10 C: 0.232, 20 C: 0.0224, 50 C: 0.00215 s.
  Cell-to-cell spread in self-discharge, % of capacity per month, by cell temperature: 25 C: 0.83, 35 C: 1.66, 45 C: 3.32.

Operations:
  The plant runs FCR; the operator schedules a charge to the top of the window every 5 days for SOC recalibration.
  Recalibration: the plant rests 30 min at 90% SOC and the BMS resets SOC from the open-circuit voltage.
  Between recalibrations the BMS counts charge. Current sensors are auto-zeroed while the contactor is open.
  The HVAC holds the cells at 35 C. Balancing can run 8 h per day.

Firmware team (fixed):
  Cell over-voltage is confirmed after 3 consecutive scans of the whole daisy chain, then the MCU opens the string contactor in its next control cycle.
  Overcurrent trip at 154 A from the current sensor (no daisy chain in this path); above the contactor's breaking capability the BMS keeps it closed and leaves interruption to the fuse.
  Precharge: the main contactor closes when the DC bus is within 2% of the string voltage. The BMS checks the bus voltage 1.5 s after starting precharge and aborts if it has not risen. The precharge relay is rated 30 A peak. The start sequence before precharge takes 1 s.

Derived requirements to write down, each traced to the stakeholder need it comes from, with a value that follows from the data: R-SOC (maximum SOC error, %), R-TRIP (maximum over-voltage disconnect time, ms), R-PRE (maximum precharge time, s), R-BAL (minimum balancing current, mA), R-BRK (minimum DC breaking current of the string contactor, A).

Objective: minimize the BMS and protection price for the plant (monitoring chips, balancing stages, current sensor, MCU, contactor and precharge resistor for every rack). The design must meet every stakeholder need, and every requirement that follows from them and from the data, whether or not it is listed here; its price must be within 5% of the cheapest design that does.
